correctness.rationale: The two ensembles have the same graph-distance compatibility and normalization 2b, but different measures on terminal configurations. From the cited exact formulas, put A(t)=sum_{k=b}^{2b−1} t^k(1+t); it increases strictly from 0 to 2b and the equilibrium root solves A(t)=1. Logarithmic differentiation at that root gives S=b/[t A'(t)], reproducing the stated reciprocal and giving monotone algebraic bounds. My independent /workspace/branches/audit_ladder.py used dyadic root brackets, those polynomial derivative bounds, and the composite midpoint rule rather than the frozen trapezoid code. For the dynamic term it enclosures e^v for v=−P_b or v=2H_b−1/b by the positive Taylor series with directed integer rounding, bounds the remainder by 7/6 times term 41 for 0<=v<=6, and reciprocates. From |P'|<=2b, |P''|<=2b² and e^P<=1, the scaled midpoint error is at most b³/(4N²). For N=4096 every exact comparison was strict: S−J<0 at b=1,...,9, with S_9−J_9 in [−0.0001030740,−0.0000813480], and S_10−J_10 in [0.0026574377,0.0026872401]. Separately q=t^b satisfies −log q=2b artanh(q(1−q)); q(1+q)<=1 bounds q uniformly away from 1. For x=2bq, this yields x=O(log b), then x+log x=log(2b)+O(log² b/b), and monotone inversion gives x=W(2b)+O(log² b/b). Substitution in 1/S gives 1+1/x+O(q). The derivative of x/(1+x) is O(1/log² b) near W(2b), giving the asserted O(log b/b) error. Expanding 1/(1+W) with W(z)=log z−log log z+O(log log z/log z) gives the stated second coefficient. This verifies the first crossing, not that all b>=10 have the same strict ordering. The cited dynamic limit is background, not a new deduction from the ten comparisons.
